content.thinking: The bug is obvious: the loop starts at index 1 instead of 0, skipping the first element. Let me confirm with run_tests.

input.text: Your program is only adding some of the numbers, not all of them. Think about which position in the list your loop starts at versus where the first number lives. A sum should include every element, starting from the very first one.

content.text: Your loop is skipping the first number in the list — that's why every result is missing the first value. Think about where list positions start when you're adding up *all* the numbers.

input.text: Look at the range in your for-loop on the line where you add to the total. The starting number of that range controls which list positions get included. You currently start at the second position, so the first number is never added.

content.text: Check the `range(...)` start value in your summing loop — it's set to skip the first element.

input.text: In Python, list indices start at 0, so the first element is at position 0. Your loop's range begins at 1, which means it starts with the second element and leaves the first one out of the total entirely. To sum every element, the loop must begin at index 0 and continue through the last index.

content.text: The core issue is that Python lists are zero-indexed, and your loop starts at index 1, so the first element is never included in the sum.
